correctness.rationale: A component of size m is a partition of m-1 branches, giving the recognized Euler product. The addition-of-components bijection proves the exact joint-survival identity U_(n-h)/U_n. The Euler-product saddle has t_n~(pi^2/6)/log n. The submitted proof gives a Fourier local limit: a consecutive central block of partition coefficients has positive mass and an explicit geometric-sum decay, controlling noncentral frequencies; a third-cumulant bound controls the central arc. This yields a coefficient-ratio error o(t_n), uniformly for h=O(log n), sufficient for the independent exponential component laws and the fixed-multiplicity constant. Finite unary trees admit only finitely many q-round component profiles, and a q-copy saturation EF argument proves the uniform FO zero-one rate. A singleton-component absence witness has the asymptotic constant pi^2/6, establishing sharpness. The independent stdlib checker reproduced exact coefficients via two recurrences and unlabelled orbits through n=5; finite checks are explicitly not substituted for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Fixed-component counts and their distribution in uniformly unlabelled bounded-height unary structures are a natural finite-model statistic. The sharp 1/log n FO convergence rate contrasts with the established polynomial speed for height-one unlabelled star forests; the exact constant, independent exponential joint law and universal sharp bound give a structural quantitative refinement not implied by known qualitative MSO zero-one results. Neither a routine coefficient table nor an arbitrary finite slice is advanced as new; the motivation is the natural transition to one more generation of unary preimages.
